content: WAL is the canonical SQLite multi-process config: PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL is persistent (stored in DB header, set once), readers don't block writer and writer doesn't block readers, still only ONE writer at a time; busy_timeout needed because WAL still returns SQLITE_BUSY on connection-close cleanup, crash recovery, and read-to-write lock upgrades (which return BUSY immediately without waiting - needs app-level bounded retry). Pragma order matters on first open: busy_timeout FIRST (the WAL switch itself needs a write lock, two processes racing first-open collide), then journal_mode=WAL, then synchronous=NORMAL (canonical WAL pairing: no fsync per commit, power loss may lose last txn but cannot corrupt; index is rebuildable). Constraints: all processes same host (no NFS/network FS), cannot open read-only WAL DBs. Auto-checkpoint at 1000 pages default; PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE) on daemon shutdown keeps -wal small. sqlite-vec vec0 tables work under WAL: llama-stack PR #5428/#5442 added exactly WAL+busy_timeout=5000+synchronous=NORMAL to their sqlite-vec provider to fix multi-worker 'database is locked'; sqlite-vec issue #40 (fixed alpha.37) was unfinalized vec0 statements blocking multi-connection writes - INSERT vec0 always inside explicit transactions. SIF connection.py currently sets NO pragmas (verified in repo, local).
